headline: Discussed state plug-in solar bill, new city solar permitting rules, and fleet electrification; June minutes moved to October.
summary: Updates covered a governor candidate's plan to end the net-zero commitment, a fleet assessment that evaluated more than 150 vehicles, and state permitting rules. Council liaisons may attend, but they cannot take part in formal deliberations unless the meeting is cross-posted with the Finance Committee.
decisions: Moved approval of June minutes to the October agenda.
Allowed both City Council liaisons to attend, but not take part in formal deliberations unless the meeting is cross-posted with the Finance Committee.

transcript:
Clean Energy Advisory Committee

Wednesday, September 16, 2026

6:30 pm - 8:00 pm

2026 NOV 12 P 12:39

Meeting location: Beverly Public Library and Virtual

CEAC members present - Jordan, Nancy, Sarah, Fred, Kira, Tom, Amy

1. **Chair Kira Fabrizio calls meeting to order at 6:32pm**

2. **Roll Call and Welcome**
   a. Attendees
      - CEAC members: Sarah Cullinan, Kira Fabrizio, Fred Hopps, Tom Keeley, Nancy Schalch, Amy Smith, Jordan Stutt
      - Others: Councilor Kathleen Feldman, Councilor Scott Houseman, Ibrahim Lopez-Hernandez, Kevin O'Reilly, Bruce Egan, Guy Bellino, David Mahood, Matt Simon

3. **Vote to approve prior meeting minutes**
   a. Approval of June minutes will be added to October agenda

4. **Meeting minutes for future CEAC meetings**
   a. Jordan taking minutes for September
   b. Kira to circulate minutes sign up sheet for upcoming meetings – participants to volunteer as recorder
   c. Google meet audio recordings to be used to complement written minutes

5. **Committee Composition**
   a. Next appointment to come from Mayor
   b. Must have four City Council appointments, three Mayoral appointments

6. **City Council Liaisons**
   a. Ok for both City Council Liaisons (Houseman and Feldman) to be on, but they cannot participate in formal deliberations unless meeting is cross-posted with Finance Committee

7. **Annual Committee Focus-setting**
   a. CEAC has been most impactful when we focus on small number of initiatives and each initiative has a clear, dedicated lead
   b. Kira has met w/ Darlene, Julia, and Ibrahim with the City of Beverly to solicit input, and will continue to meet monthly w/ Ibrahim
   c. Potential issue areas for CEAC
      - Fleet Electrification
         - City received fleet assessment from National Grid
         - Incentives available for vehicles, chargers, and infrastructure to support cost-effective transition
         - Jordan to be focus area leader, Matt to participate
      - Legislative Policy
         - Tracking and engaging on state-level legislation with direct implications for Beverly
         - Fred and Kevin volunteering to lead focus area
      - New City ordinance for solar and batteries
         - Will establish new review process for projects
         - CEAC can be a resource to support that process and help deliver positive outcomes
         - Tom volunteering to be focus area leader
      - Planning Committee Engagement
         - Might be too much to take on at the moment
         - Can use CEAC engagement on siting ordinance as a test for this kind of role for CEAC in planning efforts
      - Community Engagement
         - Kira to raise this with Ibrahim and Julia
         - CEAC can support City with community engagement on City projects

8. **City Updates**
   a. Candidate for Governor (Minogue) is proposing to end net-zero commitment and increase funding to cities that do away with stretch code
   b. Fleet Assessment findings & next steps
      - Received report in June
         - Evaluated 150+ vehicles
            - 141 have options for electrification
            - Recommends 84 for conversation
   c. Clean Energy Siting Permitting
      - All municipalities must provide optional expedited permitting process
      - City working w/ MAPC on templates and guidelines
      - Should have this in place by October
      - If municipality doesn't get their permitting sorted in October, applicants would go through Energy Facilities Siting Board

9. **Green Transportation Update**
   a. Parking minimum policy next steps
      - Will be interesting to see how this rolls out in Salem
      - First project in Salem under new policy is now in development
      - CEAC will watch, learn, and continue to research

10. **Legislative Updates**
    a. Plug in solar
       - House and Senate reconciling language
       - Expectation is that language will be resolved and signed into law by Gov. Healey
       - Applies to relatively small solar deployments (likely up to 1,200 watts); won't dramatically shift energy demand at scale, but gives more consumers opportunity to start benefiting from solar
       - If signed into law, DPU/DOER would be responsible for public input process and implementation
          - Sarah can advise on process

11. **The Bigger Picture**
    a. EPA plans to repeal regulations on power plant emissions
    b. Pipeline closure from attack in Saudi Arabia results in reduced oil flows
    c. Chevron looking into new pipeline to bypass Strait of Hormuz
    d. Canadian wildfires caused poor air quality for much of Northeast and Midwest this summer

12. **November Meeting:** Sohier room not available on Wednesday, Nov. 18, so we will identify an alternate date or location

13. **Meeting adjourned at 7:58**
